`interface IKeyResolver`<br/>
**Package:** `dev.joid.lib.input.key.resolver` · **Module:** `core` · **Source:** [IKeyResolver.java](https://github.com/Zeldown/JOID/blob/main/core/src/main/java/dev/joid/lib/input/key/resolver/IKeyResolver.java)

Turns a key binding of your application into the key that it stands for, so that a shortcut can take that binding.

## Description

Implement it when your application stores its key bindings in objects of its own, such as a key that the user chose in the settings, and register it with [`KeyResolver.register`](/reference/input/keyresolver/#KeyResolver-method-register).
JOID asks the resolver again at every key, so a binding that changes applies at once.

## Method details

<a id="IKeyResolver-method-supports"></a>

### supports

`boolean supports(Object binding)` <span class="joid-qualifier">abstract</span>

If `true`, this resolver knows the binding.
JOID calls `resolve` only for a binding that this method accepts.

<a id="IKeyResolver-method-resolve"></a>

### resolve

`Key resolve(Object binding)` <span class="joid-qualifier">abstract</span>

Returns the [`Key`](/reference/input/key/) that the binding stands for now, compared with [`NodeKeyEvent.getKey`](/reference/events/nodekeyevent/#NodeKeyEvent-method-getKey), the key that the layout names.
A `null` key matches no key.
